question:
**Fill in the blanks: **

The Chairperson of the GST Council is the ______ of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Finance Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution of India to make recommendations on GST-related issues.
 
• The Chairperson of the GST Council is the Union Finance Minister of India as per the provisions outlined in Article 279A.
 
• The GST Council consists of the Union Finance Minister as the Chairperson, the Union Minister of State for Finance, and finance ministers from all states and union territories.
 
• The Council is tasked with making decisions on tax rates, exemptions, thresholds, and other GST-related matters, ensuring uniformity and cooperation across states.
 
• All decisions in the GST Council are taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present, with the central government having one-third of the votes and state governments having two-thirds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister:**

 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and leads the executive branch of India.
 
• While the Prime Minister plays a significant role in policymaking, they do not chair the GST Council.
 
• The Prime Minister may influence GST-related matters indirectly through overall policy direction and coordination with the Union Finance Minister.
 
 
 
• **President:**
 
 
• The President of India is the ceremonial head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Although the President appoints the Union Finance Minister, they do not have a direct role in the functioning of the GST Council.
 
 
 
• **Vice-President:**
 
 
• The Vice-President of India primarily serves as the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha (Upper House of Parliament).
 
• They do not hold any constitutional role in the GST Council or its decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is a pivotal body for ensuring uniform tax policies across India.
 
• Its establishment was crucial for the implementation of the GST, which subsumed several indirect taxes into one unified tax system.
 
• The Council ensures cooperative federalism by involving both central and state governments in tax-related decisions.
